l-002.evidence: Query seq 0 returns 6 rows in the observed window including `failed: 48` for `user.name: root` (auth_method `password` and `other`, 19:52:23–19:55:23Z) and three `failed: 4` groups for `user.name: dev.dana` / `' dev.dana'` (20:06:04–20:06:42Z), whereas all three live controls (C-14d, C-21d, C-28d) contain only success rows — `accepted: 7/21/8, failed: 0` for `svc.config-mgmt`, `svc.deploy`, or null user — and zero failure rows and no `dev.dana` or `root` user at all. Query seq 1 carries the same distinction in the `message` and `event.outcome` columns: `Failed password for invalid user dev.dana from 172.18.0.6 port 35532/46948/41960/49970 ssh2`, `Invalid user dev.dana ...`, and `pam_unix(sshd:auth): authentication failure ... user=root` (count 48), none of which appear in any control, whose only sshd auth row is `Accepted password for svc.config-mgmt` (C-28d, count 8). The distinction is carried by `user.name`, `message`, and `event.outcome` — stable fields — not by `source.ip` (172.18.0.6), which environment_notes marks unstable and which is therefore not relied on. Both decidable queries agree, so heterogeneous is false.

l-003.evidence: All three queries are `identity.*` templates (identity.access-check ×2, identity.user-authorization), which the environment notes classify explicitly as a state-and-lookup system returning current configuration or an entity record with no @timestamp bounds and therefore no control window. The payloads confirm this shape: seq 0 and seq 2 return point-in-time authorization records (`authorized: false`, `via: null`, `role: developer`, `sudo: false`, `shell: null`) for web-2 and db-1, and seq 1 returns dev.dana's user record (`enabled: true`, `realm_role: developer`, `authorized_hosts: [dev-ws-1, jump-box-1, office-ws-1]`, `sudo_hosts: [office-ws-1]`). The empty `baseline` is expected here rather than a missing measurement, since these queries have no baseline-diff semantics. All queries agree in kind, so the lead is not heterogeneous.
